title: Study under Giuffre and his clarinetist son Philip
summary: Two years with Giuffre using the Klose method, his strict teaching, and his son Dr. Philip Giuffre who played superbly.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: Now back when you were starting you say you studied more or less by yourself for say three years or something like that? Oh yeah, quite a while, yeah. And then Jewfree, how long were you under him?
Jewfree, I must have gone to him about two years. Any other teachers?

And I went through that clozé method, which was about an inch and a half thick, you know. Clozé? Clozé, clarinet method. It's a complete method. It's a great big thing. And after you go through that thing boy, you've done some playing. And the old man, Jewfree, was a stickler. He had a baton and he counted time while you played. And if you made one mistake, you start from the beginning, or he'd reach over and tap you on the fingers with his Italian accent, broken English, you know. He said, don't be such a jackass, you play right. He was a character, a fine old man, a real gentleman, you know. Incidentally he had a son who was a sensational clarinet player, who became a doctor, Dr. Philip Jewfree.
I guess he doesn't play music. No, no, he hasn't played music.

He's practicing in some country town I understand. He was an admitting surgeon at a charity for quite a while after his internship. But the guy could play clarinet, gee, I mean legitimate clarinet, you know. He was sensational. In fact when the old man was late some days, the kid would give him a lesson. He was a good guy.
